en: It seems like every week, there’s a news article claiming you should consume more antioxidants,
zh: 似乎每週都會有新聞文章聲稱你應該攝取更多抗氧化劑，

en: be it through fancy smoothies or sciencey-sounding supplements.
zh: 無論是透過花式冰沙還是聽起來很科學的補充劑。

en: This antioxidant craze goes back a long time to the 80s and early 90s when some early research suggested antioxidants could maybe protect against certain diseases.
zh: 這股抗氧化劑熱潮可以追溯到 1980 年代和 1990 年代初，當時一些早期研究顯示抗氧化劑或許可以預防某些疾病。

en: Food and supplement companies jumped on that research and have been touting the benefits of antioxidants ever since.
zh: 食品和保健品公司紛紛利用這項研究成果，並從此大力宣傳抗氧化劑的好處。

en: But the follow-up research investigating those benefits has actually been pretty inconsistent,
zh: 但後續研究對這些好處的調查結果卻相當不一致，

notes.example: Actually, we're just looking around for now.

en: and scientists aren’t totally sure why yet.
zh: 科學家目前還不完全確定原因。

en: Health food commercials will give you the impression that an antioxidant is a thing—
zh: 健康食品廣告會讓你覺得抗氧化劑是一種

en: a healthy thing you should be eating and drinking.
zh: 健康的東西－你應該吃喝的東西。

en: But chemically, the word antioxidant is actually more of an adjective than a noun.
zh: 但從化學角度來看，「抗氧化劑」一詞其實更像是形容詞，而不是名詞。

notes.example: Actually, we're just looking around for now.

en: It describes a range of chemicals and enzymes that can neutralize free radicals: compounds with single, unpaired electrons.
zh: 它描述了一系列可以中和自由基（ 含有單一未配對電子的化合物）的化學物質和酵素。

en: Free radicals can cause real havoc in our cells:
zh: 自由基會對我們的細胞造成真正的破壞：

en: altering DNA, damaging the proteins our cells need to function, and messing with the sophisticated membranes holding everything together.
zh: 改變 DNA，破壞細胞正常運作所需的蛋白質，並破壞維持細胞結構的複雜細胞膜。

notes.zh: come together：順利成形、水到渠成
notes.example: Everything came together right before the deadline.

en: And these free radicals can come from practically anywhere— from the food we eat to the air we breathe.
zh: 這些自由基幾乎可以來自任何地方—— 從我們吃的食物到我們呼吸的空氣。

notes.example: How come you didn't text me back?

en: Even sunlight can produce free radicals in our bodies.
zh: 即使是陽光也能在我們的體內產生自由基。

en: Now, our cells try to contain them by employing a large network of antioxidant chemicals and enzymes to deactivate the different types of free radicals our bodies encounter.
zh: 現在，我們的細胞會利用龐大的抗氧化化學物質和酵素網絡來抑制我們體內遇到的各種自由基，從而試圖控制它們。

en: But when the amount of free radicals being produced outpaces the rate at which our bodies can quench them, our cells enter a state known as oxidative stress.
zh: 但是，當產生的自由基數量超過我們身體清除它們的速度時，我們的細胞就會進入一種稱為氧化壓力的狀態。

en: Unfortunately, slipping into a bubble bath and decompressing with an episode of Queer Eye is not a viable way for our cells to de-stress, though that does work for my mind.
zh: 可惜的是，泡個泡泡浴，再看一集《粉雄救兵》來放鬆身心，對我們的細胞來說並不是一個可行的減壓方式，儘管這對我的精神確實有效。

en: And if our cells stay oxidatively “stressed” for long periods of time, there can be serious health consequences.
zh: 如果我們的細胞長時間處於氧化壓力狀態，可能會造成嚴重的健康後果。

en: In the 80s and 90s, scientists started gathering evidence that cancer, heart and neurodegenerative diseases, the negative side effects from aging could all be linked to damage from oxidative stress—
zh: 在 1980 年代和 1990 年代，科學家開始收集證據，證明癌症、心臟病和神經退化性疾病，以及老化帶來的負面影響，都可能與氧化壓力造成的傷害有關——

en: at least, in part.
zh: 至少部分是如此。

en: Research during that time also found that a Mediterranean diet, which is rich in antioxidants, was associated with a lower incidence of those diseases.
zh: 當時的研究也發現，富含抗氧化劑的地中海飲食與這些疾病的較低發生率有關。

en: Scientists put two and two together, and developed the hypothesis that supplementing people’s diets with antioxidants might prevent or even reverse the problems associated with these diseases.
zh: 科學家將兩者聯繫起來，提出了這樣的假設：在人們的飲食中補充抗氧化劑可能有助於預防甚至逆轉與這些疾病相關的問題。

notes.zh: come together：順利成形、水到渠成
notes.example: Everything came together right before the deadline.

en: It’s an elegant idea, but unfortunately, it’s been difficult to find support for.
zh: 這是一個絕妙的想法，但可惜的是，它很難獲得支持。

en: Researchers began by looking at how supplementing single antioxidant chemicals would affect cells grown in test tubes and saw some promising results.
zh: 研究人員首先研究了補充單一抗氧化劑化學物質會對試管中培養的細胞產生怎樣的影響，並看到了一些有希望的結果。

en: For example, studies showed that chemicals like Vitamin E could successfully act as antioxidants to reduce damage from oxidative stress in cell membranes.
zh: 例如，研究表明，維生素 E 等化學物質可以有效地作為抗氧化劑，減少氧化壓力對細胞膜的損害。

en: But when they tried to extend the benefits that they saw in cell cultures to randomized, clinical trials with real humans taking those same antioxidants, they found inconsistent effects.
zh: 但是，當他們試圖將細胞培養中觀察到的益處推廣到服用相同抗氧化劑的真人隨機臨床試驗中時，他們發現效果並不一致。

en: For instance, in a study called the Women’s Health Study published in 2005, a group of almost 40,000 women took either a Vitamin E supplement or a placebo every other day for 10 years.
zh: 例如，在 2005 年發表的一項名為「女性健康研究」的研究中，近 40,000 名女性每隔一天服用一次維生素 E 補充劑或安慰劑，持續了 10 年。

en: That is a big study population, which should enable you to see robust results.
zh: 這是一個龐大的研究人群，應該能夠讓你看到可靠的結果。與對照組相比，

en: The rates of cancer and heart disease were unchanged compared to control—
zh: 癌症和心臟病的發生率沒有

notes.zh: keep control over...：掌控某人或某事
notes.example: Staying calm helps you keep control over the conversation.

en: but researchers did observe a 24% reduction in heart-related deaths in the group who took the vitamin.
zh: 變化——但研究人員觀察到，服用維生素的組別中，與心臟相關的死亡人數

en: Except another study published in 2005 which tracked nearly 4,000 people over around 7 years found that Vitamin E supplements increased risk of heart failure.
zh: 減少了 24%。但另一項發表於 2005 年的研究追蹤了近 4000 人約 7 年，結果發現補充維生素 E 會增加

en: Which would indicate an increased risk of heart-related mortality—the opposite of what the first study showed.
zh: 心臟衰竭的風險。這表明心臟相關死亡風險增加——與第一項研究

en: And such contradictory claims about antioxidant supplements are so common in the field that it’s virtually impossible to take the findings of any individual study at face value.
zh: 的結果相反。關於抗氧化劑補充劑的這種相互矛盾的說法在該領域非常普遍，以至於幾乎不可能完全相信任何一項

en: In fact, a meta-analysis of 78 randomly controlled trials, with a combined sample size of almost 300,000 people of various health backgrounds, found antioxidant supplements to have no net beneficial effect.
zh: 單獨研究的結果。事實上，一項針對 78 項隨機對照試驗的統合分析（總樣本量近 30 萬名來自不同健康背景的人）發現，抗氧化劑補充劑沒有淨益處。

en: The one exception for supplements is that a combination of three antioxidants moderately reduce the risk of age-related eye disease.
zh: 補充劑的唯一例外是，三種抗氧化劑的組合可以適度降低與年齡相關的眼部

en: Which… yay. It’s something, we guess.
zh: （對照上方英文字幕跟讀）

en: Despite the lack of reliable evidence for antioxidant supplements, though, many studies have found that people who follow diets containing fruits and vegetables rich in antioxidants have lower incidence of diseases related to oxidative stress.
zh: 疾病風險。那……太好了。我們猜，這算是某種東西吧。儘管缺乏關於抗氧化劑補充劑的可靠證據，但許多研究發現，食用富含抗氧化劑的水果和蔬菜的人，患有氧化壓力相關疾病的幾率較低。

en: So we can see benefits from antioxidant supplements in a Petri dish.
zh: 因此，我們可以在培養皿中

en: And we can see benefits from antioxidant-rich diets in people.
zh: 看到抗氧化劑補充劑的益處。我們已經看到富含抗氧化劑的飲食

en: But we can’t seem to demonstrate any benefit from antioxidant supplements in people.
zh: 對人體有益。但我們似乎無法證明抗氧化劑補充劑對人體有任何益處。

en: It could be a simple problem of dosage.
zh: 這可能只是劑量的問題。

en: We may be over- or under-administering these antioxidants, so they’re not doing the job we want.
zh: 我們可能過度或不足地使用了這些抗氧化劑，所以它們沒有達到我們想要的效果。也可能是因為

en: It could also be that our cells compensate for the elevated antioxidant levels from supplements by slowing down their own antioxidant production, so overall, in our bodies, the levels don’t change.
zh: 我們的細胞會透過減緩自身抗氧化劑的產生來補償補充劑帶來的抗氧化劑水平升高，因此，總體而言，我們體內的抗氧化劑水平不會改變。或許只是因為單一抗

en: Or maybe it’s just that individual antioxidants are not effective at protecting against disease in larger organisms.
zh: 氧化劑對大型生物體抵抗疾病的效果並不好。

en: Instead, we may need a wide variety of antioxidants, rather than just one at a time.
zh: （對照上方英文字幕跟讀）

en: You know how we said that our bodies use a variety of antioxidants?
zh: （對照上方英文字幕跟讀）

en: Naturally, that’s true of fruits and veggies too.
zh: 相反，我們可能需要多種多樣的抗氧化劑，而不是一次只補充一種。你們知道我們之前說過，我們的身體會利用多種抗氧化劑嗎？當然，水果和蔬菜也同樣如此。這

en: And that might help our bodies deal with the wide variety of free radicals we naturally encounter.
zh: 或許有助於我們的身體應對我們自然而然遇到的各種自由基。每種

en: Each antioxidant compound acts a little differently.
zh: 抗氧化化合物的作用機轉略有不同。

en: So if someone has an excess of a particular free radical, giving a high dose of the wrong antioxidant could be like giving a band-aid to someone with the flu.
zh: 因此，如果某人體內某種自由基過量，給予高劑量的錯誤抗氧化劑就好比給流感患者貼創可貼一樣

notes.zh: don't take this the wrong way：別誤會我的意思（說真話前超實用緩衝句）
notes.example: Don't take this the wrong way, but the second version reads better.

en: It’s just not the right treatment.
zh: 。這根本不是正確的治療方法。也

en: It might also just be that studying nutrition is just plain hard.
zh: 可能只是因為營養學本身就很難。

en: And we have a whole video on why that is, which we’ll put a link to at the end of the video.
zh: 我們專門製作了一個影片來解釋原因，影片結尾會附上連結。

en: Whatever the reason, antioxidant supplements don’t have much evidence to recommend them.
zh: 無論出於何種原因，目前尚無太多證據支持使用抗氧化劑補充劑。

en: That’s even though we know the chemistry, and even though we know having them in your diet is linked to beneficial effects!
zh: 即使我們了解其中的化學原理，即使我們知道在飲食中加入它們會帶來有益的效果！

en: Our bodies are complicated and science is weird about connecting dots sometimes, but that’s why we do it: to really know what we know.
zh: 我們的身體很複雜，科學有時很難將各種點連結起來，但這正是我們做科學的原因：為了真正了解我們所知道的。

en: And right now, we just don’t know about those antioxidant pills.
zh: 而現在，我們對那些抗氧化藥丸還一無所知。

en: Thanks for watching this episode of SciShow.
zh: 感謝收看本期科學秀。

en: Our amazing patrons help us do what we do every day, and that includes making this video.
zh: 我們了不起的贊助人幫助我們每天完成工作，這其中也包括製作這段影片。

en: Thank you to all of our patrons!
zh: 感謝所有顧客！

en: If you’d like to join them, you can do that at patreon.com/scishow.
zh: 如果你想加入他們，可以造訪 patreon.com/scishow。
